chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from his father, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said:

I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) about a man who struck a pregnant woman with his leg, so she dropped what was in her belly as dead. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was a nutfah (seed/embryo), then upon him is twenty dinars.' I said, 'So what is the limit of the nutfah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that which, when it falls into the womb and settles in it for forty days.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if she dropped it and it was an 'alaqah (clot), then upon him is forty dinars.' I said, 'So what is the limit of the 'alaqah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that which, when it falls into the womb and settles in it for eighty days.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if she dropped it and it was a mudghah (lump of flesh), then upon him is sixty dinars.' I said, 'So what is the limit of the mudghah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that which, when it falls into the womb and settles in it for one hundred and twenty days.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if she dropped it and it was a nasamah (formed person) with bones and flesh, distinguished limbs, and the spirit of intellect had been blown into it, then upon him is a complete diyah (blood money).' I said to him, 'What do you think if it transforms in her belly to a state, would it be with a spirit or without a spirit?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'With a spirit, other than the old life which is transferred in the loins of men and the wombs of women. And if it were not that there was a spirit in it other than the life, it would not have transformed from one state to another in the womb, and there would not have been a diyah upon the one who kills it while it is in that state.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensation for miscarriage caused by physical trauma?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated financial compensation (diyah) for miscarriage, distinguishing between early embryonic stages and the post-soul infusion period. It highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that the 'blowing of the soul' (nafkh al-ruh) occurs at 120 days, marking the transition from partial compensation to a full human life's value, supported by the Imam's explanation that the soul's presence is evidenced by the fetus's developmental transformation.
